(2) rerun PR #81's dagu-inflight-resume-after-kill fixture (SIGKILL mid-step, then attempt recovery) but hold at least 120s after the kill before the recovery attempts -- past both of Dagu's documented thresholds (lock_stale_threshold default 30s, heartbeat stale_threshold default 90s) -- plus an immediate post-kill history/ps check, since the original PR #81 run only waited ~1-2s and was recorded as inconclusive/narrowed by a Codex review to 'inconclusive' rather than 'refutes_incumbent'.

results.inflight_resume_after_kill: CORRECTED FROM AN EARLIER DRAFT OF THIS RECEIPT, which overstated this result as conclusively settling self-healing; that overclaim is retracted here. No dagu scheduler was ever started in this fixture (only `dagu start`/`dagu retry` were invoked directly), and zombie-process detection is a scheduler responsibility (the 2.17.0 binary's own --help documents SCHEDULER_ZOMBIE_DETECTION_INTERVAL, a 45s default zombie-detection interval, and a 3-consecutive-stale-check requirement before a zombie is declared, on top of the 90s heartbeat stale threshold -- roughly 90+3x45=225s minimum with a scheduler running, which this test never ran long enough to reach even if a scheduler had been present). Separately, the `dagu start --run-id <same>` refusal ('dag-run ID ... already exists') is a duplicate-run-ID check, not a staleness/lock check, so it was always going to fail regardless of the hold duration and is not evidence about the thresholds; only the `dagu retry --run-id` refusal ('already running... socket=/tmp/@dagu_inflight_<hash>.sock') is a relevant staleness-adjacent signal. What this check actually establishes: past the 120s hold (exceeding the 30s lock_stale_threshold and the 90s heartbeat stale_threshold individually), with NO scheduler running, a manual `dagu retry --run-id` on a SIGKILLed run is still refused and `dagu history` still reports status 'running' 2m31s after the kill. Whether a running scheduler's zombie-detection loop would independently reclaim and allow recovery of this run (which needs on the order of 225s of scheduler uptime past the kill, not 120s, and a scheduler process this test did not start) remains UNTESTED and INCONCLUSIVE, same as PR #81 recorded, not settled by this rerun.

limits: The inflight-resume-after-kill self-healing question remains INCONCLUSIVE, not settled, for both 2.16.6 and 2.17.0: no run in this fixture (nor PR #81's) ever started a `dagu scheduler` process, and scheduler-driven zombie detection (the only documented self-healing mechanism) needs roughly 90s heartbeat-stale plus 3 consecutive ~45s zombie-detection checks (about 225s) of scheduler uptime past the kill to fire at all. This receipt only shows that a bare `dagu retry --run-id` without a scheduler is refused at 120s post-kill; it does not show whether a scheduler would recover the run, at 120s or at 225s+.

The `dagu start --run-id <same>` refusal captured in this run is a duplicate-dag-run-ID error ('already exists'), not a staleness/lock-timeout error, and was misread as threshold-relevant evidence in an earlier draft of this receipt; it is retained in the results verbatim but is not treated as supporting the timing claim.

A manual `dagu stop` or manual deletion of the stale socket file before retrying was still not tried in this rerun (same limitation PR #81 recorded); whether either of those recovers the run past the threshold remains untested.
